mainEntity.name: Is this an AI receptionist for roofers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Kaico Voice is an AI receptionist built for roofing companies. It answers 24/7 with your company name, captures the address and the damage the caller describes, books the inspection onto your Google Calendar, transfers active-leak calls to your cell and sends you a text or email summary after each call. It tells callers it is an AI, and you can hear it yourself at (918) 359-2644.

mainEntity.name: Can it keep up with call volume after a hail storm?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. It is software, not one person at a desk, so a post-storm surge does not turn into a hold queue or a busy signal. It answers every call, 24/7, including the ones that come in at 9 pm while you are still tarping roofs. Every booking lands on your calendar and every call gets a transcript you can read that night.

mainEntity.name: What happens when a caller has an active leak?

acceptedAnswer.text: Calls about water actively coming into a house are treated as emergencies. The receptionist transfers real emergencies to a human on your team, and you decide which number it rings. Everything else gets booked or taken as a message so your phone only interrupts you when it should.

mainEntity.name: Can it answer insurance and adjuster questions?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and it does not pretend to. Questions about claims, deductibles, supplements, or adjuster meetings are taken down as detailed messages for a human on your team to return. The caller hears that a person will call them back, and you get the details in the transcript instead of a vague voicemail.

mainEntity.name: Will homeowners know they are talking to an AI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The honest test is to hear it yourself. Call (918) 359-2644. That line is the receptionist itself, live, answering the way it would answer your customers. Most callers just want the roof dealt with, and a fast, competent answer beats a voicemail box every time.

mainEntity.name: How fast can we be live before the next storm?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your receptionist is answering calls within 7 business days once we have your hours, services and call-forwarding details. You also tell us your service area, what you inspect for free, and which calls should transfer to a person. If storm season is already here, 7 business days is still faster than hiring, training, and scheduling a receptionist.
